note: Each suggestion carries the decision the reviewer must make before any implementation.

suggestions.title: Separate the two strategy ID spaces before anything else is joined
suggestions.problem: `data/derived/bets.csv` (line_lab build, IDs S1..S11, 16,439 bets) and `data/derived/gates_results.csv` (pipeline build, IDs S01..S18) both use S-numbered strategy IDs for different rules. `S10` means 'Rest edge of 4+ days to the away team' in one build and something else in the other, so any join on ID silently mixes the two.
suggestions.proposal: Prefix every strategy ID with its build (LL- and PL-), add a `build` column to both ledgers, and make the hub builder refuse to join two ledgers unless the namespaces differ.
suggestions.effect: Removes a whole class of wrong-number defects before more data arrives.
suggestions.risk: Breaks any downstream file that hard-codes S01..S18; must be done with a checked migration.
suggestions.decision: Adopt the namespacing now, or freeze both ledgers and never join them?
suggestions.evidence: Reproduced in this session: scoring S10 in one ledger against the other build's published ROI gives -0.0873 instead of +0.0430, a 13-point error.

suggestions.title: Record a pre-registration commit hash for every strategy
suggestions.problem: Rules can be added or edited after their result is known. Nothing in the build prevents it, and the multiple-comparison correction assumes advance registration.
suggestions.proposal: Store the commit hash that introduced each rule, show it on the strategy page, and fail the build if a rule has no registration commit older than its test output.
suggestions.effect: Makes the statistical claim honest and auditable.
suggestions.risk: Some historical rules predate the repository; they must be marked 'unregistered' rather than back-filled.
suggestions.decision: Registrations from now on only, or re-register the historical rules and re-test?
suggestions.evidence: Official statistics guidance states post-hoc pairwise comparison does not control the overall error rate.

suggestions.title: Ship the availability view as an officially-sourced layer, with depth left blank
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for backup-deficiency analysis, but no official depth chart could be reached, so any string-level number would be invented.
suggestions.proposal: Publish exactly what is official: game status, practice status, roster status and reserve moves, aggregated per club and per unit with declared weights. Keep a clearly separated 'depth: not available' column.
suggestions.effect: Delivers the usable half of the brief without fabricating the other half.
suggestions.risk: A reader may mistake the availability index for a depth measure; the labelling must stay blunt.
suggestions.decision: Is the official-layer-only version acceptable as v1, or is a licensed depth feed required first?
suggestions.evidence: 254 official player rows transcribed and validated this session; the official depth-chart URL returned 404.

suggestions.title: Pre-register the injury hypothesis before acquiring any historical injury data
suggestions.problem: The obvious next step is to test whether injury news beats the closing line. Done in the wrong order it will produce a false edge, exactly as the eighteen earlier rules did: none passed, and the best raw result did not survive multiplicity control.
suggestions.proposal: Write the rule, the sample, the pass bar and the kill criterion first; commit them; only then obtain data. Test one hypothesis, not a family.
suggestions.effect: The only way the result will mean anything.
suggestions.risk: The pre-registered rule may simply fail, which is the expected outcome and still valuable.
suggestions.decision: Fund the data acquisition now, or wait until a single hypothesis is agreed?
suggestions.evidence: All 18 rules in gates_results.csv have verdict FAIL; the best raw ROI (+8.41%, S14) carries q=0.288 and failed gate G4, multiplicity control.

suggestions.title: Keep this decision register as a standing, dated page
suggestions.problem: Questions, answers and gaps are scattered across six executive summaries written by six sessions.
suggestions.proposal: Maintain one register with an owner, a status and a source per row. Add a 'what changed since the last review' section.
suggestions.effect: A reviewer can see what is decided and what is still open in one place.
suggestions.risk: Becomes stale if it is not updated with each snapshot.
suggestions.decision: Adopt this page as the canonical register, or keep per-session summaries?
suggestions.evidence: Five executive-summary files at the repository root carry partially overlapping claims, plus six separately served dashboard builds.

suggestions.title: Decide the reward scheme explicitly, or remove the word 'reward'
suggestions.problem: The brief asks for rewards for top strategies. No pool, sponsor, currency, payout rule or jurisdiction exists, and a reward promise can create legal obligations.
suggestions.proposal: Choose one: (a) funded pool with published terms and an eligibility rule, (b) reputation-only leaderboard with no money, (c) drop the competition framing.
suggestions.effort: Low to decide, high to operate
suggestions.effect: Removes an unanswerable question from the critical path.
suggestions.risk: Option (a) needs legal review before any announcement.
suggestions.evidence: The published leaderboard has zero reward-eligible strategies; the eligibility rule requires all gates to pass and none did.

suggestions.title: Replace the single ROI ranking with a three-axis board
suggestions.problem: A single ROI column ranks the luckiest rule first. The repository computes a week-block bootstrap interval, a permutation percentile and a shrunk ROI, but they sit on different pages from the ranking, and the raw-ROI leader is the rule whose data source is unverified.
suggestions.proposal: One table with ROI, shrunk ROI, permutation percentile, sample size and required sample, sortable, with an explicit tiebreak rule.
suggestions.effect: Makes the competition honest and much harder to misread.
suggestions.risk: More columns is more to read; the default sort must be stated.
suggestions.decision: Default sort on shrunk ROI, or on the permutation percentile?
suggestions.evidence: Median bets needed at the shrunk edge across the 18 rules is 14,300, against a largest existing sample of 2,555.

suggestions.title: Add a weekly refresh with a recorded HTTP status per source
suggestions.problem: The site is a snapshot. Injury pages change hourly and can disappear.
suggestions.proposal: A small job that re-checks each official URL, records the status and timestamp, and flags any source that stops resolving. It must not fail the site build when an external site is down.
suggestions.effect: Turns 'verified on a date' into a maintained claim.
suggestions.risk: A flaky external site could spam flags; the job must distinguish 'source down' from 'repo broken'.
suggestions.decision: Weekly, or before every game day?
suggestions.evidence: This session found a live 404 for the official depth-chart page, which a status check would have caught automatically.

suggestions.title: Measure player-level pair correlations once a prop-line source exists
suggestions.problem: The correlation work covers only team-level markets. Prop combinations are documented by mechanism but not measured, because no prop-line archive exists.
suggestions.proposal: Acquire a prop-line archive with timestamps, then measure the same phi statistic on the pairs already listed, and compare against each operator's same-game-parlay repricing.
suggestions.effect: Turns the prop framework from a hypothesis list into evidence.
suggestions.risk: Operators reprice SGPs, so a measured correlation may not be a measured edge.
suggestions.decision: Is a licensed prop feed worth the cost before the team-level question is settled?
suggestions.evidence: Operator rules explicitly reserve the right to restrict or reprice correlated legs.

suggestions.title: Consolidate six overlapping builds behind one canonical dashboard
suggestions.problem: The repository serves six generations of dashboards from one GitHub Pages root, each with its own numbers and its own executive summary. A reader cannot tell which is current.
suggestions.proposal: Keep the others archived and immutable, but make one page the only entry point, with a single change log and a 'superseded' banner on the rest.
suggestions.effect: Removes the largest source of reader confusion.
suggestions.risk: Other sessions own those directories; consolidation must be done by whoever owns them, not by overwriting.
suggestions.decision: One canonical dashboard, or keep all six live and clearly dated?
suggestions.evidence: README.md lists six bodies of work served from this one repository, from six different sessions.

suggestions.title: Replace the unprovenanced weather columns or drop them
suggestions.problem: The wind-based rule (S14, 'Wind 15+ mph: unders') ranked first on raw ROI at +8.41%, but its own source field reads 'wind field from the pinned dataset (UNVERIFIED, no source field)'. A top-ranked rule resting on an unprovenanced column is unusable.
suggestions.proposal: Either obtain station-level observations with identifiers, or remove weather from the feature set and mark those rules retired.
suggestions.risk: Retiring a rule reduces the apparent size of the strategy library.
suggestions.decision: Fund a weather source, or retire the weather rules?
suggestions.evidence: gates_results.csv rank 1 is S14 with roi 0.0841 and rationale source 'wind field from the pinned dataset (UNVERIFIED, no source field)'.

suggestions.title: Add a change log and per-page 'last verified' stamps
suggestions.problem: Every page in the dashboard carries the same single snapshot date, so a reader cannot tell which claims were re-checked in this session and which were inherited from an earlier one.
suggestions.proposal: Per-source verification date rendered next to the source, plus a single change log page.
suggestions.risk: Requires disciplined updating, or the stamps become noise.
suggestions.decision: Per-source dates, or a single snapshot date?
suggestions.evidence: All 34 sources in the register share one snapshot date, though they were last confirmed by different sessions on different days.
